profile.name: Maria Lopez
profile.goal: Help the next generation of women lawyers get their start

steps.text: Offer a 20-minute call to a student on your path
steps.why: One conversation can change a student's first year.

steps.text: Nominate a junior colleague for a speaking slot
steps.why: Sponsorship moves careers faster than advice.

achievements.reason: Sandra Day O'Connor practiced as an attorney before she became the first woman on the U.S. Supreme Court in 1981.

achievements.text: Argued my first case before the 9th Circuit
achievements.reason: Elena Kagan clerked for a federal Court of Appeals judge early on. She later became the fourth woman on the Supreme Court.

achievements.text: Founded a legal aid clinic for immigrant families
achievements.reason: Shirin Ebadi, a lawyer and former judge, founded the Defenders of Human Rights Center in Iran and won the 2003 Nobel Peace Prize.

achievements.text: Won a landmark housing discrimination case
achievements.reason: Ruth Bader Ginsburg spent her life in the law, and sat on the U.S. Supreme Court from 1993 to 2020.

achievements.text: Named partner at a civil rights firm
achievements.reason: Before she was First Lady, Michelle Obama graduated from Harvard Law School and started her career at a Chicago law firm.

achievements.text: Testified before the state senate on fair housing
achievements.reason: Barbara Jordan, an attorney, was the first Black person elected to the Texas Senate since Reconstruction.
Janet Reno led the U.S. Justice Department as attorney general from 1993 to 2001.

achievements.text: Elected chair of the county bar association
achievements.reason: Kathleen Kennedy Townsend, an attorney, became the first woman to serve as Maryland's lieutenant governor.

achievements.text: Mentored my first Made of Her student
achievements.reason: Malala Yousafzai has spent her life fighting for girls' education, and won the Nobel Peace Prize at 17.

achievements.text: Spoke at a high school career day about law
achievements.reason: In 1968 Shirley Chisholm became the first Black woman elected to the U.S. Congress.

steps.text: Read one Supreme Court opinion summary on Oyez
steps.why: Learn how judges reason before you argue.

steps.text: Ask a mentor on your path for a 20-minute call
steps.why: Lawyers who went first can save you years.

steps.text: Sign up for your campus pre-law society meeting
steps.why: Peers on the same path keep you going.

achievements.text: Joined my college's mock trial team
achievements.reason: Sonia Sotomayor grew up in the Bronx and became the third woman to serve on the U.S. Supreme Court.

achievements.text: Emailed a law professor about research
achievements.reason: Michelle Obama grew up on Chicago's South Side and went on to Princeton and Harvard Law School.

achievements.text: Got an A on my constitutional law midterm
achievements.reason: Ruth Bader Ginsburg spent 27 years interpreting the Constitution on the U.S. Supreme Court.
